about: The intake question bank. Claude walks the owner through it one question at a time (references/questionnaire.md is generated from this file by tools/build_questionnaire.py), and the intake workbook's Questions tab lists the same questions. 'maps_to' names where the answer lands in payroll_config.json or period.json.

sections.title: Before we start
sections.intro: Have these handy if you can: one or two recent payroll registers, an offer letter or comp plan for each kind of role, the list of reports you pull from your booking/POS system, and an export of your roster from your HR or payroll system. None of it is required to begin; the interview works from memory and fills gaps later.

questions.q: In one or two sentences, how does payroll work today, from closing the period to people getting paid?
questions.why: Shows which steps are manual, who does them and where errors slip in.

questions.q: What went wrong in past payrolls that you never want to see again?
questions.why: Every past mistake becomes a check. Most real payroll errors are omissions (a missing export, a dropped person), not arithmetic.
questions.follow_up: Was it caught before payday? By whom?

questions.q: Who will run this each period, who reviews the numbers, and who submits to the payroll system?
questions.why: The review workbook and sign-off lines are written for these people.

sections.title: The business, its entities and locations
sections.intro: Overtime is counted per legal employer, and minimum wage is set by where the work happens. Getting entities and locations right first prevents two of the most expensive mistakes.

questions.q: What is the business called, and how often do you pay (weekly, every two weeks, twice a month, monthly)?
questions.why: Sets the pay frequency, which drives salary per period.

questions.q: How many days after the period ends is payday?
questions.why: Sets how much time the export, review and fix loop has; final-pay deadlines for people who leave can be sooner.

questions.q: What day does your workweek start? (Check your payroll system; it is often Sunday.)
questions.why: Weekly overtime is judged on this fixed 7-day week, not on the pay period.

questions.q: List each legal entity (LLC or corporation) that employs people. Are all locations under one entity or separate ones?
questions.why: Hours at two locations of the same employer are added together for overtime. Separate entities are generally counted separately; confirm with your payroll provider if ownership is shared.

questions.q: List every location: a short code, its name, city and state, and which entity runs it.
questions.why: Every hour and every sale is tied to a location for minimum wage, overtime and cost reporting.

questions.q: What is the minimum wage at each location today, and when does it next change? Some cities and counties set their own.
questions.why: Non-service time and sick pay are often paid at minimum wage, and every workweek must clear it. Oregon, for example, has three regional rates.

questions.q: How does each location appear in your booking/POS reports and in your HR system (names, numbers, codes)?
questions.why: So a report labelled '0102' or 'Eastside Salem' lands on the right location.

questions.q: Does your payroll system track locations as departments, divisions or cost centers? What are the codes?
questions.why: Lets the payroll file split pay by location.

sections.title: Systems
sections.intro: The engine never logs into anything. It reads exports you download. These answers decide which export layouts to expect and which payroll file to produce.

questions.q: Which booking/POS system do you use? Which reports do you pull for payroll today?
questions.why: Each report becomes one canonical input file. Claude maps the columns once and records them.

questions.q: Which HR system holds your roster and pay rates (BambooHR, HiBob, Paylocity, ADP, Gusto, a spreadsheet)?
questions.why: Picks the HRIS on-ramp that turns its roster and time-off exports into inputs.

questions.q: Which payroll system pays people? Do you upload hours, dollar amounts, or both?
questions.why: Picks the outbound file layout.

questions.q: Do staff clock in and out? In which system? Do service providers clock, or only the front desk?
questions.why: Decides whether hours worked come from the clock or from service time plus recorded non-service time.

questions.q: In your payroll system, what are the exact names of each pay type you upload (for example 'Commission', 'Credit Card Tips')?
questions.why: An upload with a pay type name that is off by one character is rejected or, worse, mapped to the wrong earning.

questions.q: Which employee number does your payroll system use? Is it the same as the HR system's?
questions.why: The payroll file must carry the number the payroll system knows.

sections.title: Roles and who is who
sections.intro: A role is a way of being paid. Most spas have four or five.

questions.q: List each role (for example massage therapist, esthetician, stretch therapist, nail tech, stylist, front desk, manager).
questions.why: Every rule hangs off a role.

questions.q: For each role: is it paid per hour of service, per service performed, a percent of service revenue, hourly on the clock, or salary?
questions.why: The pay basis decides which inputs the role needs and how its hours are counted.

questions.q: Which service categories does each service role perform (massage, facial, stretch, nails, hair...)?
questions.why: A dual-role person's services are paid at the rate of the role that matches the category.

questions.q: Which roles receive tips?
questions.why: If a tipped role has no tips file, the run stops instead of paying zero tips.

questions.q: Is any salaried role exempt from overtime? Is any manager paid hourly?
questions.why: Exempt salary is not checked for overtime; non-exempt staff always are.

questions.q: How do your HR system's job titles map to these roles?
questions.why: Lets the HRIS import assign roles without hand edits.

questions.q: Does anyone hold two roles (for example massage therapist and esthetician)? At what rate is each paid?
questions.why: Their services are split by category and paid at each role's rate; their incentives follow the role that earned them.

questions.q: Does anyone work at more than one location? Which is their home location?
questions.why: Their hours are combined for overtime across locations of the same employer, and time off is charged to the home location.

questions.q: Does anyone have a pay deal that differs from the standard plan (a ramp, a guaranteed rate, a special spiff)?
questions.why: Special deals are the most common source of missed pay. Each one becomes an override or a rate row with dates.
questions.follow_up: Where is it written down? When does it change next?

questions.q: Are there contractors or booth renters? (They are outside this payroll and should not appear in it.)
questions.why: Keeps them out of the employee checks.

questions.q: Do names in your POS differ from legal names (nicknames, 'NICK: Last, First', capitalization)?
questions.why: Name aliases stop one person appearing as two.

sections.title: Service pay
sections.intro: For service providers this is most of the paycheck. The single most damaging error in spa payroll is paying service hours from the wrong column or the wrong report.

questions.q: Which report is the single source of truth for service hours? Is it actual service time, never scheduled or bookable time?
questions.why: Scheduled or bookable time includes empty gaps and overstates pay. The engine pays only the service-hours column of the service report.

questions.q: Does that report total each provider's service hours and service count? (Those totals are recorded each period and checked.)
questions.why: If the mapped rows do not add up to the report's own totals, the run stops.

questions.q: What is each provider's service rate, and where is it kept?
questions.why: Rates come from the HR export or a rates file, with an effective date for every change.

questions.q: Do upgrades, add-on minutes or extensions count as service time?
questions.why: Upgrade codes often carry real service minutes that must be paid to the right role.

questions.q: How are refunds, comps, no-shows and late cancellations handled for pay?
questions.why: Refunded lines are negative rows; a paid no-show fee may or may not pay the provider.

questions.q: When two providers share a service (couples, four-hands), who gets credit for the hours?
questions.why: The report must credit each provider their own time.

questions.q: Do rates change by step, tenure or performance during the year? How are you told?
questions.why: A missed step increase is an underpayment that compounds. Each change is a dated rate row.

questions.q: If a provider clocks in, is the time between clients paid separately? (Some states require it for piece-rate pay.)
questions.why: California-style rules need non-productive time paid on its own.

sections.title: Non-service time
sections.intro: Lobby, training and meetings are where piece-rate staff are most often underpaid, because the time lives in a different report from the services.

questions.q: Which kinds of non-service time do you pay: lobby/floor, training, being trained, training others, meetings, cleaning, travel, waiting?
questions.why: Each kind gets its own rule; a kind with no rule stops the run rather than paying zero.

questions.q: At what rate is each paid: minimum wage, the person's own rate, a fixed rate, or their regular rate?
questions.why: The rate basis per role and kind.

questions.q: Which report holds that time? Is it the same report for every location?
questions.why: Becomes the time entries input; it is the only place training and lobby hours come from.

questions.q: Are there caps (for example 4 lobby hours a month)? What happens above the cap?
questions.why: Caps are a policy; hours worked above them must still be paid. The engine pays what was recorded and flags it.

questions.q: What pay type name does each kind go under in your payroll system (for example Training covers both trainee and trainer)?
questions.why: Pay type names must match the payroll system exactly.

questions.q: Do any staff work in a state that requires paid rest or recovery periods for piece-rate workers?
questions.why: Those periods are paid at the regular rate, not minimum wage.

sections.title: Add-ons and enhancements
sections.intro: Add-on reports usually show the customer price. Paying that price instead of your spiff rate is a classic overpayment, and an add-on code nobody listed silently pays nothing.

questions.q: List every add-on or enhancement code your POS uses and what you pay the provider for each one. Include the ones that pay nothing.
questions.why: Every code gets a rate, even $0. A new code with no rate stops the run until you decide.

questions.q: Do codes share a prefix (for example CBD, CBD-SCENTED, CBD-UNSCENTED all pay the same)?
questions.why: One prefix rule covers the family.

questions.q: Which roles earn add-on pay? Does an esthetician's enhancement pay differently from a massage add-on?
questions.why: Role gating per incentive.

questions.q: Do any add-ons pay only certain people (a certification, a pilot)?
questions.why: Restricted rates pay only the named people; everyone else's units are listed as unpaid.

questions.q: Does the add-on report show a code, a description, or 'CODE: Description'?
questions.why: Matching works on the code before the colon.

sections.title: Retail, memberships, packages and gift cards
sections.intro: Sales incentives are often monthly or seasonal. The question is always: which sales, by whom, over which dates, at what rate.

questions.q: Do you pay commission on retail? What percent, to which roles, and is it paid every period or monthly?
questions.why: Monthly incentives are paid only on the month-end run, over the whole month.

questions.q: How are membership sales paid? Per sale, tiered (first 5 at one rate, then another), or a percent?
questions.why: Tiers are counted per person per location unless you say otherwise.

questions.q: Which membership transactions do NOT pay: renewals, upgrades, transfers, conversions, cancellations within a grace period?
questions.why: Exclusions are explicit rules, so they are applied the same way every time.

questions.q: Do gift card or package sales pay commission? Always, or only in seasonal windows (holidays, Mother's Day)? Exact dates?
questions.why: Windows are set per period; sales just outside a window are reported, not silently dropped.

questions.q: Is the commission base the sale amount, the quantity, or something else? Which report column?
questions.why: Paying on a percentage column instead of the dollar column has produced commissions of a penny.

questions.q: Do managers earn an override on their location's sales? On which sales, at what rate?
questions.why: Location-credit incentives pay named people on the whole location's total.

questions.q: If someone sells at a location where they did not work any hours that period, should they still be paid there?
questions.why: This edge case dropped real commissions before. The engine pays the seller wherever the sale happened.

questions.q: Are refunds and chargebacks clawed back from commission? Within what time?
questions.why: Refund rows reduce the base; the engine never claws back below zero without your adjustment.

questions.q: Are card tips paid on the paycheck in full to the person who earned them?
questions.why: Tips pass through untouched and are reconciled to the tips report total.

questions.q: Do you pool or share tips (for example with the front desk)? On what formula?
questions.why: Pooling needs an explicit rule and is regulated; confirm it with your payroll provider or counsel first.

questions.q: Are cash tips declared through payroll? Only reported, or also paid?
questions.why: Declared cash tips are usually reported for taxes, not paid again.

questions.q: Do you add a service charge to bills? Is any of it paid to staff?
questions.why: A service charge is not a tip; if shared it is wages and belongs in the regular rate.

questions.q: Which report gives tips per provider per day? Does it include prepaid tips or tips on gift cards?
questions.why: The tips report is also proof of who worked; someone with tips and no pay is a red flag.

sections.title: Sick time, PTO and holidays
sections.intro: A missing time-off export pays nobody's sick hours, and every other check still passes. The engine will not run without either the rows or a statement that nobody took time off.

questions.q: How is sick time paid for each role? (Piece-rate staff are often paid at minimum wage or their regular rate; check your state.)
questions.why: Sick pay rules by role and type.

questions.q: Do you offer PTO, vacation, holidays, bereavement or jury duty pay? To whom, at what rate?
questions.why: Each type needs a rule, or the run stops.

questions.q: Where does time off come from: your HR system's time-off report, the payroll system, a spreadsheet?
questions.why: Becomes the time-off input for exactly the pay period dates.

questions.q: Does your payroll system already pay approved time off from its own records?
questions.why: If it does, the engine shows time off in the review but leaves it out of the upload so it is not paid twice.

questions.q: For people who work at several locations, which location carries their time off?
questions.why: Time off is charged to the home location.

sections.title: Overtime and the minimum-wage floor
sections.intro: Overtime is per workweek, never per pay period, and a week that straddles two pay periods is judged on its combined hours. Commissions and non-discretionary bonuses raise the rate overtime is paid at.

questions.q: Do you have staff in a state with daily overtime, double time or seventh-day rules (for example California)?
questions.why: Loads the state's preset, which you confirm with your payroll provider or counsel.

questions.q: Do service providers ever work more than 40 hours in a week, counting service time plus lobby, training and meetings?
questions.why: Piece-rate staff earn overtime too, as a half-time premium on their regular rate.

questions.q: Are commissions, spiffs and bonuses included when you figure the overtime rate today?
questions.why: Non-discretionary incentives belong in the regular rate. Monthly ones are trued up across the weeks they were earned.

questions.q: If a week's pay ever came out under minimum wage for the hours worked, would you rather be stopped to decide, or have a make-up line added automatically?
questions.why: The floor is checked every workweek.

questions.q: When the time clock is exported, is it pulled for exactly the pay period dates (not full weeks)?
questions.why: A full-week export on a boundary week re-pays days already paid last period.

questions.q: List each manager, their annual salary (or per-period pay), and the locations they run.
questions.why: Salary per period and the cost split across locations.

questions.q: Are any managers paid a stipend for covering another location? From when, until when?
questions.why: Stipends with an end date stop on their own instead of being paid forever.

questions.q: How are manager bonuses earned? Which metrics, which thresholds, what is each worth, and how often?
questions.why: Each metric is a pass/fail rule with a weight; the pool per location is fixed.

questions.q: Where do the metric numbers come from (a scorecard report?) and for which dates?
questions.why: Recorded each bonus period as location metrics.

questions.q: Who is paid each location's bonus? Can two people both receive it in full, or is it shared?
questions.why: Recipients and shares per location, separate from who manages it day to day.

questions.q: Is the bonus discretionary (you decide after the fact) or promised in advance?
questions.why: Promised bonuses for non-exempt staff belong in the overtime regular rate.

questions.q: How do one-off items happen today: signing bonuses, referral bonuses, back pay, reimbursements?
questions.why: Each one is an adjustments row naming who approved it, so it survives a rebuild and shows in the audit trail.

questions.q: What pay type names do those use in your payroll system? Are reimbursements non-taxable there?
questions.why: A one-off that reuses a regular pay type name gets mixed into the wrong reconciliation.

questions.q: Who is allowed to approve a one-off payment?
questions.why: Recorded on every adjustment line.

questions.q: How do you learn about new hires, terminations, leaves and rate changes before payroll?
questions.why: Terminated staff still appear in POS reports; new hires may not appear in a report pulled with an old filter.

questions.q: When someone leaves, how is their final pay handled, and how fast?
questions.why: Final-pay deadlines vary by state and can be earlier than the next payday. The run reminds you each time.

questions.q: If someone is active but shows no hours, services or time off, what is usually going on?
questions.why: Silence is a warning: a filtered export, a wrong location, or a leave nobody recorded.

questions.q: Have you paid anyone off-cycle recently whose activity might show up again in this period's reports?
questions.why: Prevents paying the same commission twice.

sections.title: What you hand to the payroll system

questions.q: Can you download your payroll system's import template (hours and/or extra pay)? Please share the header row.
questions.why: Every connector profile is a starting point; your own template is the truth.

questions.q: Does your payroll system pay hours at the rate it has on file, or do you send the rate?
questions.why: If someone's rate changed mid-period, one rate on file cannot pay both; the run warns.

questions.q: Should the file be split by location or department?
questions.why: Location codes are added to each line when you need them.

questions.q: Any company code, batch ID or file naming rule the upload needs?
questions.why: Some systems (ADP paydata) reject a file with the wrong name or batch.
